messages:
maria: Quick question — for customer-facing audit exports, should 'create_deployment' and 'api_key_use' events be visible to org members, or strictly org admins?
ryan: I think org admins + owners. Members shouldn't see cross-tenant activity. We need to avoid accidental exposure. :warning:
samir: Agreed. Our current index has tenant_id on every event and we do post-query filtering, but there are edge cases with derived events (like 'shared_snapshot') where tenant linkage is indirect.
lena: For auditors (role = auditor) we planned a scoped token with audit:read limited to tenant scope. Do we want that to map to exports as well?
sec-bot: NOTE: any export that contains card numbers or email PII must be redacted per compliance. See policy: /policies/audit-export-redaction.
maria: Good call. Also KMS signing question — when we sign exported audit bundles with customer KMS, does the signing service need access to plaintext? How do we avoid giving it a global view of tenant mappings?
samir: Implementation idea: use envelope keys. The export service packages events, encrypts with a per-export symmetric key, then calls KMS to sign the ciphertext and return a signature. KMS only sees metadata and the encrypted blob, not raw rows.
ryan: Sounds right. Need to ensure signing request doesn't include tenant_id in clear. Use a hashed tenant footprint in metadata: `tenant_hash = sha256(tenant_id || export_id)`.
lena: Also schema change: add `visibility_level` enum to audit_event: ["tenant_only","tenant_admins","platform_ops"] so UI/exporter can enforce policy. Will create a migration.
infra-oncall: Heads up — if visibility enforcement is at query layer, we need a middleware to enforce enforcement for internal tools/ops consoles. Otherwise platform_ops will accidentally see tenant_only events.
maria: Action items: lena opens RFC for schema + migration, samir writes KMS envelope flow doc, ryan to update token service to forbid audit:read scoping to multiple tenants in one token. I'll file infra policy to add enforcement middleware.
sec-bot: DEPENDENCY: tag this thread with #compliance-review when RFC is ready.
ryan: One more edge-case: historical exports. If we change `visibility_level` default, we must backfill or treat legacy events as tenant_only until reviewed. Add to RFC.
maria: Thanks all — I'll spin up a tiny PoC in staging: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer scoped-token" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports?tenant=T-123` and verify response contains only tenant events and the bundle is signed without plaintext tenant metadata.
lena: I can help test after I push the migration branch.
samir: I'll draft the KMS flow doc and include sequence diagram.
maria: OK closing for now. Will post RFC link here when created. :white_check_mark:
